title: Compatibility runway: phased API consolidation and client transition requirements
creator: Ravi Patel
description: High-level PRD: As part of the API Consolidation Initiative we need a clear requirements doc and migration runway enabling client libraries and integrators to move away from legacy endpoint shapes and older model aliases without service disruption. This ticket captures product requirements, acceptance criteria, phased scope changes, and the operational timeline for a coordinated client transition. The goal is a low-friction migration that preserves backward compatibility for a defined window, provides automated adaptors for common SDKs, and introduces telemetry gates to avoid customer regressions.
background_and_rationale: Over time multiple transport semantics and model aliases accumulated in the API surface. This creates operational cost, inconsistent performance guarantees, and customer confusion (multiple ways to request chat/generate/embeddings). We want to consolidate to the Unified Inference surface, reduce maintenance burden, and enable routing/fallback optimizations in the serving runtime. Rather than an abrupt removal, we will define a compatibility runway with opt-in adaptors, telemetry gates, and a graduated decommissioning to minimize customer disruption.
scope_included:
- Publish compatibility mapping for every legacy endpoint and model alias to its Unified Inference equivalent.
- Ship client-side migration helpers for official SDKs (JS, Python, Go).
- Provide server-side adaptors for high-usage enterprise tenants for 3 months of overlap.
- Create dashboards and alerting rules to track migration adoption and error spikes.
- Define and publish final cutover criteria and rollback conditions.
scope_excluded:
- Full rewrite of third-party SDKs beyond official Redwood SDKs.
- Requiring customers to migrate before feature parity checks finish.
- Backporting the compatibility layer to older runtime branches (we will support only runtime-1.20+).
goals_and_success_metrics:
- 75% of active SDK calls use the Unified surface within 60 days of GA.
- No customer-facing error rate increase >0.5% during phased migration windows.
- No more than 5 enterprise support cases caused by incompatibility per sprint during migration.
- Performance delta for converted requests stays within +20% latency and -10% throughput compared to legacy routes.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Compatibility mapping published and validated in docs. 2) JS/Python SDK migration helpers released with unit and integration tests. 3) Telemetry dashboard (migration-adoption) shows ingestion of usage signals. 4) Canary cohort (5% traffic) runs through adaptors for two full business cycles without blocking incidents. 5) Migration playbook and rollback steps reviewed and approved by SRE and Support. 6) Legal and Billing communicated impacts and agreed on transitional credits policy.
migration_steps:
1. Finalize endpoint-to-unified mapping and publish docs (week 0-2).
2. Release SDK helpers and opt-in compatibility flag (week 2-6).
3. Offer per-tenant server-side adaptors for top 30 customers and start shadowing (week 4-8).
4. Open public migration dashboard; begin phasing client-side opt-ins (week 6-10).
5. Enable automatic routing with feature flag for 5% canary (week 10-12).
6. If telemetry stable, ramp to 25% then 50% over two weeks each; monitor regressions and support volume (week 12-18).
7. Begin deprecation notice window (60 days) after 50% adoption sustained.
8. Final cutover and disable server-side adaptors after 90 days post-deprecation notice (week 24+).
rollout_timeline: Phase A (GA helpers and docs): 2025-03-01 to 2025-03-21. Phase B (canary routing and per-tenant adaptors): 2025-03-22 to 2025-04-18. Phase C (ramp and deprecation notice): 2025-04-19 to 2025-05-30. Phase D (final cutover and adaptor removal): 2025-06-30 (target). Dates are estimates and gated on telemetry and incident thresholds.
monitoring_and_telemetry: Create a migration-adoption dashboard with: 1) % traffic hitting unified endpoints by SDK/version, 2) error rate delta (unified vs legacy) per customer cohort, 3) latency and p50/p95 comparisons, 4) support ticket volume tagged for migration. Add alert thresholds: error rate spike >0.5% or latency regression above +40% p95 triggers immediate rollback and triage.
communication_plan:
- Week 0: Publish PRD and notify ecosystem via developer-announce mailing list and public roadmap.
- Week 3: Publish SDK migration guides and sample code snippets.
- Week 6: Host two live migration office hours targeted at integrators and top enterprise customers.
- Week 10: Send per-tenant migration readiness reports to top 50 customers.
- Deprecation window: 60-day public notice with pre-filled client update guides and support playbook.
- Cutover day: status page updates and real-time rollout dashboard link shared with customers.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Large-batch jobs using legacy batch-embed transport may break. Mitigation: Provide a migration adapter in the SDK that rewrites requests and a fallback grace period for bulk jobs.
Risk: Unexpected latency regressions for long-context models after kernel selection changes. Mitigation: Constrain early routing to short-context variants and expand as profiling proves safe.
Risk: Enterprise customers with strict private deployments may not accept adaptors. Mitigation: Offer on-prem adaptor recipe and dedicated SRE migration runbook.
implementation_notes:
- Engineering owners: Runtime, SDK, Console, SRE.
- Runtime work required: routing flag, compatibility handler, telemetry hooks.
- SDK work: migration helper functions, compatibility flag, backward-compatible parameter translation, and automated tests.
- Console work: migration dashboard and per-tenant readiness reports.
- Support collateral: playbook, templated e-mails, rollback contact list.
open_questions:
- What is the minimal feature parity checklist that we require before commencing tenant opt-ins?
- Should we offer temporary usage credits to enterprises that opt-in to early routing? If so, who signs off?
- Are there any regulatory customers who require extended adaptor windows beyond the default 90 days?
